risk_signals.statement: SHAHJABANK was touched by the sector-wide FY2024 asset-quality recognition event documented elsewhere in this dataset, but far more mildly than most peers and with a rapid one-year recovery. Classified Investment as % of Total Investment rose from 4.42% (FY2023) to 7.88% (FY2024) -- Volume of Non-Performing Investment nearly doubled, from 10,689mn to 21,191mn (+98.2%) -- while CAR eased only slightly from 15.06% to 14.27% (still comfortably above the 12.50% Basel-III minimum-plus-buffer) and PAT fell from 3,625mn to 1,688mn (-53.4%), pulling ROE down from 15.89% to 7.15% and EPS from 3.26 to 1.52. By FY2025 nearly all of this reversed: Classified Investment ratio fell to 4.46% (volume down to 13,080.16mn, a 38.3% one-year reduction), PAT reached an ALL-TIME HIGH of 3,679.51mn (surpassing the prior FY2023 high of 3,625mn), ROE recovered to 15.00%, and CAR held at 14.19%. This is a materially milder and faster-resolving shock than the same-year events documented for NBL (balance-sheet insolvent, CAR -5.48%), ABBANK (NPL 56.53%, CAR -3.78%), IFIC (equity down to 0.96% of assets, CAR 1.82%), ISLAMIBANK (884,350mn unprovided = 12.7x equity), and this dataset's own EXIMBANK (Gross NPI 3.64%->28.40%, ROE 10.08%->1.46%) and FIRSTSBANK (classified 3.95%->91.75%, institutional failure) -- none of which recovered within the archive's window.

FY2024's ~98% one-year jump in classified investment volume is not unprecedented for this bank: FY2018 saw a near-identical proportional shock, with Volume of Non-Performing Investment rising from 6,301mn (FY2017) to 12,723mn (FY2018), +101.9%, and Classified-Investment-minus-Specific-Provision (an unprovisioned-exposure proxy) reaching 10,278mn against Total Shareholders' Equity of 14,789mn (69.5% of equity) -- actually a HIGHER equity-relative exposure than FY2024's 13,275mn unprovisioned against 23,427mn equity (56.7%). Both episodes were followed by rapid de-escalation: the FY2018 ratio fell to 38.9% by FY2019 and 30.8% by FY2020; the FY2024 ratio fell to 26.4% by FY2025. CAR never fell below 11.54% (FY2016, its second-lowest point) in either episode or at any other point across the full 15-year series (range 11.40% FY2011 to 16.02% FY2019). Total Shareholders' Equity grew in 13 of the 14 year-over-year comparisons available; the sole exception is FY2024 itself, when equity dipped 1.40% (23,760mn -> 23,427mn) as the credit shock compressed profit available for reserve accretion while dividends continued to be paid -- it recovered to a new high (25,627.25mn) the very next year. This reads as a recurring, bank-specific credit-cycle pattern that has twice self-corrected within 1-2 years, rather than a structural deterioration.

Across all 15 years of this dataset (FY2011-FY2025), SHAHJABANK's Capital Adequacy Ratio never fell below 11.40% (its FY2011 value, under the then-Basel-II regime) and peaked at 16.02% (FY2019). Its worst point in the entire archive is barely 3 percentage points off its best, and it never approached the negative or sub-2% CARs recorded for several peer banks in this dataset in FY2024 (NBL -5.48%, ABBANK -3.78%, IFIC 1.82%, FIRSTSBANK 4.92%). Tier I Capital Ratio and Tier II Capital Ratio independently reconcile to the reported CAR in every single year (verified programmatically; the sole exception, FY2013, is a documented one-off arithmetic typo in the source PDF that this dataset corrects -- see sources.json).

This bank's own multi-year summary tables are unusually internally consistent relative to other banks already researched in this dataset. Parsing and cross-checking all 15 annual reports' 'Five Years Financial Summary' tables (each checked against up to 4 other reports' comparative columns for the same year) found only 5 genuine restatements plus 1 corrected arithmetic error, versus 85 restatements found for IFIC and 83 for ISLAMIBANK in prior sessions of this same project. The one material restatement (FY2013 Total Assets: 121,963.43mn contemporaneous vs 128,554.28mn per the FY2014 report, +5.40%) is a symmetric Other-Assets/Other-Liabilities gross-up that preserves the balance-sheet identity in both versions; the rest (FY2019 and FY2020 Tier 2 Capital, FY2023 Tier 1 Capital) are small capital-note revisions, each shifting Total Capital (Tier1+Tier2) by only 0.03%-2.73% (FY2023: 9mn/0.03%; FY2020: 480mn/1.72%; FY2019: 800mn/2.73%). A genuinely arithmetically-impossible figure was found and corrected: the FY2013 report's own printed headline CRAR of 12.56% contradicts its own Tier I (12.35%) + Tier II (1.34%) = 13.69%, corrected here to 13.69% per project convention.

The bank's own reported Return on Equity changes calculation methodology partway through the archive. For FY2011-2013, reported ROE reconciles exactly to PAT divided by AVERAGE TOTAL REGULATORY CAPITAL (Tier1+Tier2), not average book equity: e.g. FY2011 PAT 1,168mn / avg(FY2010 Total Equity Core&Supplementary 7,747mn; FY2011 9,183mn) = 13.80%, matching the reported 13.80% exactly, while PAT / average BOOK equity for the same year would give 15.93%. From FY2014 onward (PAT 747mn / avg(11,698mn; 10,951mn) = 6.60%) the bank's reported ROE matches average BOOK equity exactly, and continues to do so in every year through FY2025 (verified: FY2025 PAT 3,679.51mn / avg(25,627.25mn; 23,426.97mn) = 15.00%, matching reported 15.00% exactly). ratios_timeseries.json standardises FY2011-2013 to the average-book-equity convention (15.93% / 19.70% / 12.67%) for cross-bank comparability, while quarterly/<YEAR>_Q4.json preserves the bank's own reported figures for all years with this methodology difference documented in each affected year's metric_note.

Newly visible from the FY2014-2025 Q1/Q2/Q3 interim data added 2026-08-26: SHAHJABANK's Q4-standalone profit contribution (full-year PAT minus 9-month cumulative PAT) has been shrinking for four consecutive years and turned outright negative in three of them, a pattern completely invisible from the Q4-only annual series alone. FY2022: cumulative PAT reached 3,450.38mn by 30-Sep, full-year PAT of 3,525mn implies a Q4-alone contribution of only ~74.62mn (the smallest of that year's four quarters, though still positive). FY2023: cumulative PAT reached 3,676.26mn by 30-Sep -- HIGHER than the eventual full-year figure of 3,625mn, implying a Q4-alone loss of approximately -51mn (the first negative quarter in this pattern). FY2024: the most severe case in the dataset -- cumulative PAT reached an interim high of 4,048.19mn by 30-Sep-2024 (quarterly/2024_Q3.json), then FULL-YEAR PAT came in at only 1,688mn (quarterly/2024_Q4.json), implying a single-quarter Q4 swing of approximately -2,360mn, i.e. Q4 alone erased more than half of the profit the bank had already booked for the year. FY2025: cumulative PAT of 3,913.77mn by 30-Sep fell to a full-year 3,679.51mn, a Q4-alone swing of -234.26mn -- smaller than FY2024's collapse but still negative, and still consistent with the same multi-year pattern. In every one of these four years, Operating Profit itself grew every single quarter with no exceptions (FY2022 Q4-alone Operating Profit +1,001.70mn; FY2023 +1,297.43mn; FY2024 +2,115.67mn; FY2025 +3,448.09mn -- all positive), so the swings are entirely a BELOW-THE-OPERATING-PROFIT-LINE phenomenon (tax and/or loan-loss provisioning concentrated at year-end audit finalization), not a revenue or cost-control problem. This directly corroborates and adds intra-year timing detail to the already-documented fy2024_credit_shock signal: the FY2024 shock was not spread evenly through the year, it was booked almost entirely in the audited Q4/annual figures, after three quarters of unaudited interim results that looked like a record year in progress.

Newly visible from the FY2014 Q1/Q2/Q3 interim data (sourced from the FY2015 annual report's comparative column, since FY2014's own report predates this disclosure -- see sources.json): SHAHJABANK's already-known FY2014 full-year low point (PAT 747mn, the lowest in this dataset's 15-year archive) conceals a cumulative NET LOSS position through the first half of the year. Cumulative PAT was -184.08mn at 31-Mar-2014, worsened to -598.70mn at 30-Jun-2014 (a Q2-alone loss of approximately -414.62mn), then swung sharply positive with a Q3-alone gain of approximately +814.60mn (cumulative reaching +215.90mn at 30-Sep-2014), before a final Q4-alone contribution of approximately +531.10mn closed the year at the already-documented 747mn. As with the FY2022-2025 Q4-compression pattern (see other risk_signal), Operating Profit itself grew every single quarter of 2014 with no exception (607.06mn / 1,213.80mn / 1,836.63mn cumulative through Q1/Q2/Q3, rising further to 2,333mn for the full year) -- the H1 loss position was entirely a below-operating-profit-line event (heavy provisioning and/or tax charges concentrated in H1, partially reversed in Q3), not a revenue or operating-cost problem. This is consistent with the bank's own historical_context note that FY2013-2014 followed directly on from Bangladesh's 2010-11 capital-market crash ('the 2011 debacle'), and shows the stress extended further into the bank's income statement, and later into the year, than the annual-only figures previously suggested.

insights.historical_context: Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC grew its Solo balance sheet from Total Assets of 107,229mn (FY2011) to 427,425.71mn (FY2025), a 3.99x increase over 14 years (10.38% CAGR), with only one contraction year in the entire archive -- FY2013, when Total Assets fell 8.18% and Total Investment fell 10.89% year-on-year, coinciding with the aftermath of Bangladesh's 2010-11 capital-market crash, referenced directly in the bank's own FY2015 annual report's Directors' Report as the '2011 debacle' (verbatim: 'last five years since 2011 debacle, virtually failed to bring [stability to the capital market]', annual_reports/SHAHJABANK/shahjabank-annual-report-2015.txt line 3098). Profitability grew unevenly but resiliently: PAT ranged from a low of 747mn (FY2014) to an all-time high of 3,679.51mn (FY2025, surpassing the prior FY2023 high of 3,625mn), interrupted twice by classified-investment shocks of near-identical proportional size (FY2018 and FY2024, both roughly doubling classified investment volume year-on-year) that the bank resolved within 1-2 years each time without CAR ever falling outside its historical 11.40%-16.02% band; equity grew in 13 of the 14 year-over-year comparisons, dipping only in the FY2024 shock year itself (-1.40%) before reaching a new high in FY2025. Investment-to-Deposit Ratio (the Islamic-banking LDR equivalent) has stayed within a 79.62%-93.00% range across the full archive and has never come close to Bangladesh Bank's current 92% Islamic-bank IDR ceiling since Basel-III-era reporting began (90.32% in FY2018 is the highest value recorded from FY2015 onward; FY2019-FY2025 itself never exceeds 87.47%), in contrast to this dataset's FIRSTSBANK, which breached the same ceiling at 118.45% (FY2023) and 122.25% (FY2024) shortly before failing. As a Shariah-based bank, SHAHJABANK reports 'Investment' rather than conventional loans and 'Classified Investment' rather than NPL, consistent with EXIMBANK and FIRSTSBANK elsewhere in this dataset; unlike those two S. Alam-Group-linked Islamic banks, none of SHAHJABANK's FY2011-2025 annual reports surfaced any related-party-lending governance red flags, regulatory forbearance letters, qualified audit opinions, or going-concern paragraphs. UPDATE 2026-08-26: Q1/Q2/Q3 interim data (sourced from each annual report's own embedded 'Evaluation of Quarterly Financials by the Audit Committee and Board' table, FY2014-2025) now gives intra-year visibility the Q4-only series lacked -- see the recurring_q4_profit_compression_2022_2025 and fy2014_h1_cumulative_loss_position risk_signals. Both the FY2014 low point and the FY2024 shock, previously known only as full-year numbers, turn out to have been driven by concentrated below-operating-profit-line events (provisioning and/or tax) landing in specific quarters (H1-2014; Q4-2024) rather than by any deterioration in the bank's core, steadily-growing Operating Profit.

(4) FY2022 report: Solo Total Property and Assets = 339,818,866,156 (line ~23729) vs Consolidated = 342,727,632,326 (line ~23376) -- stored value (339,819mn) matches Solo. sources.note: VERIFIED PRESENT in 11 consecutive years' own annual reports: FY2015-FY2025 (a prior research pass had found only FY2015-2022 + FY2024 -- this session additionally confirmed FY2023 (heading 'EVALUATION OF QUARTERLY PERFORMANCE', line ~16978, easy to miss because it doesn't literally contain the phrase 'Evaluation of...Quarterly' the other years use) and FY2025 (embedded in a two-column page layout that scrambles naive text search). CONFIRMED ABSENT in FY2011-2014's own reports: FY2011's Corporate Governance compliance checklist (using the older 2006 SEC notification, items 1.1-1.4 only) has no quarterly-variance item at all; FY2012-2014 use a newer notification (dated 7 Aug 2012) whose checklist item 1.5(ix) ('If significant variance occurs between Quarterly Financial performance and Annual Financial Statements...') is answered with only a checkbox ('N/A' or a bare compliance tick) and NO data table -- confirmed by direct inspection of all four years' compliance-checklist sections. BONUS FY2014 DATA: although FY2014's own report has no table, the FY2015 report's table carries a full '01 Jan 14 to ...' comparative column with real FY2014 Q1/Q2/Q3 data -- used as the sole source for quarterly/2014_Q1-Q3.json, cross-validated against the independently-sourced quarterly/2014_Q4.json (Five Year Summary-derived): Dec-31-2014 figures match exactly (Total Assets 126,758.38 vs 126758mn, PAT 747.21 vs 747mn, Equity 11,698.50 vs 11698mn, EPS 1.02, NAV/share 15.92 -- all reproduce). FY2011-2013 remain genuine gaps: no report in this bank's whole archive carries interim data for those years, under either the checkbox-only years' own tables or any later comparative column (the table format itself did not exist before FY2015). BASIS CONFIRMED SOLO in every one of the 11 own-report years, matching this bank's main Q4/annual series: each year's own 31-Dec column in this same table reproduces the already-validated quarterly/<YEAR>_Q4.json Solo figures exactly (e.g. FY2018 Total Assets 243,659.89 vs 243660mn; FY2022 339,818.87 vs 339819mn; FY2025 427,425.71 vs 427425.71mn to the cent) in every single year checked (2015-2025) -- no Consolidated-basis contamination found anywhere in this table. CROSS-VINTAGE VALIDATION (per-year table checked against the following year's comparative column, same methodology as the annual series): FY2015, FY2018, FY2020, FY2022, FY2024 fully stable (zero difference, including per-share figures). FY2016, FY2019, FY2021 stable on all absolute BDT-value figures; per-share figures (EPS/NAV per share/NOCFPS) retrospectively restated in the following year's comparative column due to intervening bonus-share issuances (same BAS-33 pattern already documented for the annual series' EPS, now confirmed to extend to Q1/Q2/Q3 granularity and to NAV/share and NOCFPS as well) -- largest swing FY2018's comparative-in-FY2019 (~9-10% reduction, tracking FY2019's ~10% bonus issue); absolute totals (assets, equity, deposits, investment, income, expenses, PAT) are NEVER affected by these per-share restatements. FY2017's Dec/full-year-only column (not Q1/Q2/Q3) shows two already-partially-known issues: Total Deposits 145,382.48->146,348.23 (+0.66%, matches the already-documented annual restatement exactly) and a Net Investment Income/Non Investment Income reclassification (4,441.06->4,576.80 and 2,428.73->2,292.99, opposite-signed, +/-135.74, net zero at Operating Profit 3,327.92 unchanged) -- closely tracks the already-documented 'Investment Income' +136mn/+1.06% annual restatement, now also visible at this finer granularity; FY2017's own Q1/Q2/Q3 figures are unaffected. FY2019's Dec-only column reproduces the already-documented ~111mn Deposits/Assets divergence exactly. FY2021: trivial 0.01 rounding in Mar-21 Operating Expenses (988.84 vs 988.83), immaterial. FY2023: a small, isolated restatement of ONLY the Mar-23 column's per-share figures in FY2024's comparative (EPS 0.99->0.97, NAV 21.14->20.52, NOCFPS 12.83->12.45; Jun/Sep/Dec-23 unaffected) -- immaterial, likely a technical weighted-average-share correction. All contemporaneous (own-report) figures were kept in quarterly/<YEAR>_Q1-Q3.json per project convention; every restatement above is recorded here rather than silently reconciled. INTRA-YEAR FINDING (see insights.json for full detail): decomposing each year's cumulative PAT into standalone quarters reveals SHAHJABANK's FY2024 full-year PAT of 1,688mn conceals a strong first three quarters (cumulative PAT reached an interim high of 4,048.19mn by 30-Sep-2024) followed by a single-quarter Q4 net swing of -2,360.19mn -- entirely a below-operating-profit-line event (Operating Profit itself grew every single quarter of 2024, Q4 included) consistent with a concentrated year-end provisioning catch-up. A milder version of the same Q4-compression pattern recurs in FY2022 (+74.62mn, smallest quarter of the year but still positive), FY2023 (-51.26mn, first negative Q4) and FY2025 (-234.26mn) -- a 4-year escalating trend not visible from the Q4-only annual series alone. A similar (but not identical -- Q1/Q2 rather than Q4) below-the-line swing produced a cumulative NET LOSS position through 30-Jun-2014 (-598.70mn) before a large Q3 reversal (+814.60mn) brought the year back to its already-known 747mn full-year profit.

sources.note: ACCESS: sjiblbd.com's primary domain is behind a BotGuard JS captcha wall (action="https://sg-sgp-xe1.botguard.net/captcha") that blocks plain curl/wget for both the listing page and every file under it -- confirmed not a filename issue, the landing page itself returns a 'Security check required' challenge to curl. WORKAROUND: the Q1 file was retrieved successfully via the bank's own unwalled mirror domain, sjibplc.com (identical file/directory layout, no captcha observed); the H1 file was not yet present on that mirror as of retrieval, so it was instead retrieved via the WebFetch tool directly against the primary sjiblbd.com URL, which succeeded where curl did not (WebFetch appears to use a different fetch path that the BotGuard challenge does not block) -- both files verified as genuine PDFs via `file` before use. BASIS: SOLO/SEPARATE, taken from the pages explicitly headed 'Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC.' (distinct from the earlier 'Shahjalal Islami Bank PLC. and its Subsidiary' Consolidated pages in the same PDF) -- verified per project standing instruction rather than assumed, matching this bank's established all-Solo convention (see reporting_basis field and the FY2015-2025 interim entry above). PROOF: each Solo Balance Sheet's own 31-Dec-2025 comparative column (Total Property and Assets 427,425,708,361) reproduces the dataset's already-validated quarterly/2025_Q4.json Solo figure (427,425.71m) to the taka. EXTRACTION: both PDFs are scanner output (pdftotext extracted 0 lines on every page of both documents, confirmed via pdfinfo/pdftotext -layout); rather than OCR (tesseract), figures were read directly and visually from clean 300dpi page renders of the Solo statements -- the scanned typeset tables are cleanly legible at this resolution, and this is more reliable than OCR for a document this size (24 pages). No classified-investment/NPL breakdown or Capital Adequacy (CRAR) disclosure exists anywhere in either 24-page filing (confirmed by reading through to the final numbered note in each) -- a genuine feature of the filing, not a research gap. VALIDATED: balance-sheet identity and full P&L waterfall (Total Operating Income - Expenses = Profit before Provision - Total Provision = PBT - Tax = PAT) reconcile exactly to the taka in both quarters. The H1 filing's P&L additionally discloses a bonus discrete Apr-Jun 2026 column (Q2-alone): PAT 1,843,525,776, EPS 1.66 -- cross-validated against Q1's cumulative PAT (1,262,274,184): sum = 3,105,799,960, matching the H1 filing's own cumulative PAT (3,105,799,959) to within BDT 1 rounding. Full detail in bank_financials/SHAHJABANK/quarterly/2026_Q1.json, 2026_Q2.json.
